articles.title: Liverpool 4-3 Villarreal: Ngumoha Stars as Mac Allister Scores Twice
articles.summary: Liverpool 4-3 Villarreal: Rio Ngumoha Inspires Anfield Comeback as Reds Survive Late ScareRio Ngumoha delivered another compelling reminder of his outstandin...
articles.body:
Liverpool 4-3 Villarreal: Rio Ngumoha Inspires Anfield Comeback as Reds Survive Late Scare

Rio Ngumoha delivered another compelling reminder of his outstanding potential as Liverpool recovered from a disastrous start to beat Villarreal 4-3 in a dramatic Champions League encounter at Anfield.

The 18-year-old winger registered two assists and caused constant problems for the visitors, helping Andoni Iraola's side overturn a two-goal deficit and maintain their perfect record in Europe.

Alexis Mac Allister scored twice, Ronald Araujo was also on target and Florian Wirtz opened his account for the season. However, Liverpool's defensive vulnerabilities ensured an uncomfortable finish.

Liverpool Punished for Poor Opening Against Villarreal

Iraola made six changes to the side that beat Brentford, with Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola and Wirtz among those named on the bench.

Liverpool struggled to find any rhythm during the opening half-hour and were punished for some particularly poor defending.

Virgil van Dijk was responsible for the opening goal after failing to deal with Renato Veiga's long ball. His attempted header back towards Alisson lacked sufficient power, allowing Georges Mikautadze to intercept and finish.

Nathan Saliba was afforded far too much space to play a straightforward pass through Liverpool's defence, with Sergi Cardona racing clear and calmly beating Alisson.

The travelling Villarreal supporters were celebrating a remarkable start, while Liverpool looked disorganised and vulnerable whenever the visitors attacked.

Mac Allister provided a much-needed response in the 36th minute, heading home from Kostas Tsimikas' corner.

Ngumoha then produced a moment of real quality shortly before the interval, lifting a perfectly weighted pass into the path of Araujo, who finished to restore parity.

It was a remarkable recovery considering how poorly Liverpool had started.

Ngumoha Changes Game as Liverpool Take Control

Iraola made a tactical adjustment at half-time, introducing Wirtz for Araujo and moving Ryan Gravenberch to right-back.

Liverpool immediately looked more purposeful in possession, with Ngumoha continuing to exploit the space against Cardona.

The teenager's contribution to Liverpool's third goal was particularly impressive.

He accelerated beyond the Villarreal defender before delivering an inviting ball across goal for Mac Allister to convert from close range.

It was the kind of direct, decisive attacking play that has made Ngumoha such an exciting prospect.

Wirtz subsequently extended Liverpool's advantage with a composed left-footed finish, finally registering his first club goal of the campaign.

His introduction brought greater fluidity to Liverpool's attacking play and offered further encouragement after a frustrating start to his season.

Tani Oluwaseyi converted following a delivery from Ayoze Perez to reduce the deficit to 4-3, ensuring Liverpool faced another nervy conclusion.

Iraola's players eventually held firm to secure their third successive Champions League victory.

Liverpool Individual Performances Highlight Strengths and Weaknesses

Ngumoha was comfortably Liverpool's standout performer.

His two assists demonstrated his growing understanding of when to take defenders on and when to release possession. Cardona struggled throughout to contain his pace and movement.

Mac Allister also deserves considerable credit. His first goal provided Liverpool with a route back into the contest, while his second completed the turnaround.

Trey Nyoni continued his encouraging development with another assured midfield display, showing composure in possession and a willingness to drive Liverpool forward.

Wirtz made a significant contribution from the bench, giving Iraola another reminder of the attacking quality available within his squad.

Defensively, however, there were several disappointing performances.

Van Dijk's mistake for Villarreal's opener was particularly uncharacteristic, while Jeremy Jacquet endured a difficult first half.

Tsimikas was also caught out positionally before improving as the match progressed.

Alisson could do little about the quality of Villarreal's finishing, although conceding three goals at home will inevitably frustrate Liverpool's goalkeeper.

Iraola Faces Defensive Questions Despite European Victory

Liverpool have now won their opening three Champions League matches, providing a strong foundation for the remainder of the league phase.

There is plenty for Iraola to be encouraged about, particularly the impact of his younger players and the attacking options available from the bench.

Ngumoha's development is arguably the biggest positive.

At 18, he is already demonstrating the confidence and decision-making required to influence important European fixtures. His performance against Villarreal will strengthen his case for further starting opportunities.

However, Liverpool cannot afford to continue giving opponents such straightforward opportunities.

The opening two goals exposed problems with defensive concentration, communication and positioning. Those issues will need addressing before Liverpool face stronger opposition later in the competition.

For now, Iraola can reflect on another European victory and a memorable individual performance from Ngumoha.

Liverpool made life unnecessarily difficult for themselves, but their response showed the attacking quality and resilience available within this squad.

articles.title: PSG's late show earns 4-2 win against Barcelona in Champions League blockbuster
articles.summary: PARIS (AP) — Paris Saint-Germain's relentless pressured led to two late goals and a 4-2 win against previously-unbeaten Barcelona in a Champions League block...
articles.body:
PARIS (AP) — Paris Saint-Germain's relentless pressured led to two late goals and a 4-2 win against previously-unbeaten Barcelona in a Champions League blockbuster on Tuesday.

A brilliant strike from Vitinha in the 81st minute and a close-range goal from Fabian Ruiz helped the two-time defending champion to a third straight win in the group stage, with 14 goals scored.

By the end, jubilant PSG fans taunted Barcelona's players with chants of "Olé" every time they touched the ball.

Not even the latest mesmerizing solo goal from 19-year-old star Lamine Yamal was enough for Barca as the Catalan club's 11-game winning run came to an end at Parc des Princes.

Yamal equalized for free-scoring Barcelona for the second time, when his goal in the 79th minute made it 2-2.

The 19-year-old forward chested down a botched headed clearance from substitute Warren Zaire-Emery and ghosted past him down the right flank with ease before stabbing the ball inside the post. It was the Catalan club's 50th goal in 12 games this season, 10 of them for Spain sensation Yamal.

Two minutes later, PSG was back in front as inspirational midfielder Vitinha controlled the ball with his chest on the edge of the area and slammed a powerful shot past Joan García into the bottom corner.

Désiré Doué had scored PSG's opening goal with a fine effort late in the first half, while his corner was headed in by Lucas Hernandez in the 72nd.

Victory softened the blow of injuries to Ousmane Dembélé, the Ballon d'Or holder, and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who both went off.

Right back Havi Espart ran through unopposed and struck a low shot into the bottom corner to make it 1-1. ___

articles.title: ‘We learned a lot’ – Hansi Flick talks Barcelona’s Champions League defeat to PSG
articles.summary: The boss felt the hosts were the better team.
articles.body:
Barcelona boss Hansi Flick says his team can learn a lot from their 4-2 Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday.

The loss is Barcelona's first of the season after a quite brilliant start to the campaign. Flick says it was a great game but that the Champions League holders "are a better team" right now.

"It was a fantastic match. In the end, PSG showed that they are a better team than us. We lost this match, but we learned a lot from it," he said. "They have a lot of quality in transition. We tried to defend against them, we did it well, but in those last fifteen minutes we weren't fresh. It's not an excuse. It wasn't the best preparation for this match, but now we have to analyze it. We need to do better things in the future, but today we did some things very well."

articles.summary: Supporters of La Liga giants Barcelona have on Tuesday evening banded together, to send a collective transfer message to the club’s board.This comes after Ha...
articles.body:
Supporters of La Liga giants Barcelona have on Tuesday evening banded together, to send a collective transfer message to the club's board.

This comes after Hansi Flick's troops were condemned to their very first defeat of the campaign, at the hands of European champions Paris Saint-Germain.

When all was said and done at the Parc des Princes, Barca found themselves on the wrong side of a 4-2 result, despite battling back to level terms during the 2nd-half.

The real issue, beyond the result, however, was the sheer number of goalscoring opportunities which the visitors gave up over the course of the 90 minutes.

PSG racked up 22 shots all told, as the lack of depth in Hansi Flick's defensive ranks in the absence of the likes of Eric García and Jules Koundé was laid bare.

Post-match on a frustrating evening for all associated with the club, those of a Barcelona persuasion have therefore taken to social media in numbers, to send a crystal clear message to Deco and his transfer team: Sign a defender.

articles.title: NFL star challenges Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappé to a race courtesy of Thierry Henry
articles.summary: New Orleans Saints star running back Alvin Kamara has challenged Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappé to a race, following an on-air discussion with France icon...
articles.body:
Widely regarded as one of the fastest players in the NFL, New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara has challenged Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappé - arguably one of soccer's quickest players - to a race.

This unexpected but potentially thrilling matchup arose on Tuesday courtesy of French soccer icon turned CBS Sports analyst Thierry Henry.

Speaking from the CBS studio with Kamara and teammate Cam Jordan, who were pitchside in Paris ahead of PSG's 4-2 UEFA Champions League win against Barcelona, the former Barça and Arsenal striker quizzed the duo on who was the fastest - with Kamara getting the nod.

Henry then quizzed the Saints pair whether or not Kamara would be able to beat Mbappé in a race with a soccer ball at his feet, to which he replied, "Yeah…I've got it. Set it up. Look, I'm of African descent, so I think I've got a lot of football instinct in me." This immediately prompted excitement from Micah Richards and Jamie Carragher in the studio, with Henry admitting he liked the 31-year-old's "confidence."

Whether or not this race ever materializes, only time will tell. However, given that Kamara's 40-yard dash time at the 2017 Combine clocked in at 4.56 seconds, and Mbappé reportedly got up to 23.4 mph at this summer's FIFA World Cup, it could be a tight race.

But if nothing else, this chat proved a moment to remember for Kamara as it gave him the opportunity to tell 49-year-old Henry, "Thierry, honestly, I have to say I've done a lot of damage with you on FIFA, so it's good to talk to you."

It also provided Henry an excellent opportunity to subtly roast fellow analyst Richards, who asked the Saints stars what position he could have played if he'd given the NFL a try. "Waterboy," Henry immediately replied.

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

On a more serious note, Kamara suggested that the former Manchester City defender looked "like a good running back. Maybe a linebacker, a good athletic linebacker. But definitely a running back. You're bigger than me."

Asked by Richards what assets he'd need to succeed, the five-time Pro Bowler explained, "You've got to have some speed. You've got to have some vision. And then it's the stuff you've got to have that is God-given. That nobody can coach…The stuff that makes the fancy plays."

Defensive end Jordan, 37, then chimed in, commenting, "After a guy like me hits you a couple of times, you'll get used to avoiding me."

The Saints duo are in the French capital ahead of the NFL's first-ever game in Paris, with New Orleans set to take on the Pittsburgh Steelers at the Stade de France on Sunday at 9:30am ET.

New Orleans heads into the game third in the NFC South with a 2-4 record, while Aaron Rodgers' Steelers sit second in the AFC North at 4-2.

articles.summary: El guardameta evitó una mayor derrota azulgrana
articles.body: El Barcelona perdió su primer partido de la temporada en París. Fue una derrota en mayúsculas porque el equipo de Hansi Flick encajó cuatro goles. Demasiados. La defensa azulgrana hizo aguas en numerosos momentos del partido, circunstancia que aprovechó el equipo de Luis Enrique para noquear a su rival sin piedad. Y lo peor para el Barcelona es que los cuatro goles encajados se quedan cortos para los méritos y ocasiones que tuvo el equipo galo a lo largo del partido. En total, fueron 22 remates los que efectuaron los franceses, lo que provocó que Joan García se convirtiera en el mejor jugador del equipo azulgrana. Si no es por el guardameta, el equipo de Flick habría encajado un resultado de escándalo. Joan García tuvo que realizar un total de diez paradas, alguna de ellas, concretamente dos, de enorme mérito. La primera a Ferran Torres que la hizo con la cara cuando el delantero se había quedado solo delante del guardameta. La otra fue en la segunda parte cuando sacó un remate de Hakimi. Y no hay que olvidar los dos palos que estrellaron los franceses. El de ayer fue un partido para aprender de los errores. A pesar del buen partido del portero, el Barcelona no pudo evitar que el equipo volviera a encajar goles. Con el partido frente al PSG ya son 18 encuentros en los que no es capaz de dejar su puerta a cero en la Champions. Es una faceta en la que el equipo de Flick debe mejorar si quiere ser campeón de Europa.

articles.title: Foden thrilled after clinical AEK Athens display
articles.summary: Phil Foden expressed his elation after scoring a treble in our 5-1 UEFA Champions League victory over AEK Athens and expressed his hunger for even more goals...
articles.body:
Phil Foden expressed his elation after scoring a treble in our 5-1 UEFA Champions League victory over AEK Athens and expressed his hunger for even more goals.

Elliot Anderson poked us ahead with his first goal for the Club before Foden rifled in a second shortly after the half-hour mark in our 150th fixture in the prestigious competition.

Stavros Pilios pulled one back for AEK Athens seven minutes after the interval before Foden's pass found Rayan Cherki to slot into the bottom corner and give us some breathing space.

Foden then took centre stage again, firing into the top corner for his brace, before completing his hat-trick from close-range, making it four goals and one assist in four days for the Englishman.

"I enjoyed that a lot," began Foden in an interview after the game. "The lads were great again. We showed determination again, it wasn't pretty at times. We were giving sloppy passes away.

"But, we stuck at the game plan and we kept going and in the end we broke them down. Overall I'm delighted. [My favourite goal is] probably the second to be honest. The way it went in.

"I'm delighted to score goals now, I'm a forward so I have to keep scoring and helping the team. It'll only do good for my confidence.

"Slowly but surely [getting back to my best], still got a long way to go. I'm going in the right direction. Scoring along the way definitely helps.

I've just got to keep working hard and try to be as best as I can for the manager and for the team. Especially when I changed into the false 9 role, I really enjoyed it a lot. In between the lines and in the pockets where I like to be and linking the play. I really enjoyed that role tonight."

The victory saw five debutants for City in the Champions League, with Floyd Samba, Allan, Ryan McAidoo, Vitor Reis and Kaden Braithwaite all getting their first taste of European football.

Foden believes they all deserved their chance and confirmed he's passing on all of his knowledge to the youngsters in the squad.

"Just trying to help them as best as I can, along with the captains, like Ruben and Erling," he continued. "Trying to help the young ones.

"It shows the trust the manager has. We've got a lot of injuries at the moment and he's not scared to use the young lads.

"They've been playing really well so they deserved to play tonight. I'm really happy for them."

articles.title: Manchester United: Michael Carrick wants clean sheets to help turn season around, starting at Como
articles.summary: Manchester United boss Michael Carrick needs more clean sheets as he looks to change his team's fortunes, as they take on Como in the Champions League.
articles.body:
"You're dead right. I can't argue with that."

Michael Carrick's response was to the point.

The question that prompted it in his pre-match news conference at a rain-lashed Giuseppe Sinigaglia stadium in Como concerned his side's failure to keep clean sheets.

It was put to Carrick that it would help if United could manage some shutouts, and he was asked if he had figured out the problem.

United have kept the opposition out just once in 10 games this season, against Azerbaijan champions Sabah FK last month.

"There's definitely parts of our game we have to improve to make things easier. I am fully aware of that," said Carrick, whose side take on Como in the Champions League on Wednesday.

The problem goes further than this season though.

They managed six clean sheets in Carrick's 17 matches in charge last term, including two in their final three games. Prior to that they had only managed two all season, part of an overall tally of nine in 63 games under his predecessor Ruben Amorim.

It is an extreme comparison given solid defence was the bedrock of Arsenal's Premier League title triumph, but the Gunners, who face Bayern Munich in Germany on Wednesday, have recorded seven clean sheets in 11 matches this season.

Continuity of selection would presumably help Carrick achieve defensive stability.

It has proved virtually elusive so far. Only once has Carrick been able to name the same back four, when Diogo Dalot, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Luke Shaw started the victory against Ipswich at Old Trafford on 30 August and kept their places for the trip to Everton the following week.

Carrick described his fitness update before the Como encounter as "a mixed bag".

That was largely based on him saying Netherlands defender Matthijs de Ligt was "fit and ready" after 11 months on the sidelines with the back injury that required surgery in May.

Yet De Ligt was on the bench at Leeds on Sunday when Martinez went off with the thigh injury that prevented him travelling to Italy, and instead Carrick turned to Noussair Mazraoui, usually a full-back, for the central slot.

United's defensive resources are stretched thinner as Leny Yoro is ruled out through suspension. Shaw is still not fit and is expected to be out for "a little bit longer" than the 10 days Kobbie Mainoo is going to miss, which could mean the left-back won't return until after the November international break.

Will Amass be the sixth left-back this season?

To many observers, the Manchester United left-back situation was one that could have been anticipated and should have been addressed in the summer.

The fact United spoke to Manchester City about Algeria international Rayan Ait-Nouri on deadline day suggests they did view it as a potential issue.

After starting all 38 Premier League games last term and the first three this, Shaw has played only twice since, and the number of games missed could reach double figures before the 31-year-old returns.

When Diogo Dalot lined up at left-back against Leeds, he became the fifth different player to start there for United in six games.

Aside from Shaw, none of the quintet could be regarded as a natural left-back.

However, after it was suggested Martinez's post-match outburst following the defeat by Atletico Madrid was partly down to 20-year-old Ayden Heaven playing at left-back, sources did point out the youngster played more often in that role than in the centre during his youth days at Arsenal.

It was also suggested in the summer that United's coaching team did not believe 19-year-old Harry Amass, who was Shaw's stand-in during pre-season, was yet at the right level.

Amass' single appearance so far this season, as a substitute for the final 18 minutes against Sabah, backs up that view, although Carrick has countered it.

"He's right in contention," Carrick said.

"At some point, young players need an opportunity. It's just finding the right time.

"Sometimes it's because there's an unfortunate thing happened to somebody else. Sometimes it's just you're doing so well we have to give you a chance.

"All the young players are in a similar boat. There's maybe four, five, or six of them trying to make that next step in terms of getting into the team and trying to start games, and Harry's definitely one of them."

We made best of transfer window - Carrick

The failure to sign competition for Shaw is a stick that has been used to beat Carrick and sporting director Jason Wilcox.

There is sympathy amid the agent fraternity for Wilcox, who was given a budget to work to that many in the game felt was inadequate to address United's needs.

There is a theory that the £50m spent to acquire Andrey Santos from Chelsea should have been diverted elsewhere.

With Santos sitting next to him as he spoke to the media on Tuesday, it was hardly a topic Carrick was going to engage with.

"When we've got injuries at different stages, we can always look at what could have been done and where we could have improved," Carrick said.

"I spoke to you about making the best of the transfer window in the situation we had. This man next to us [Santos] was a big part of that. I'm delighted to have him.

"We had to make decisions in the summer. We did what we could do and made the best of it."

articles.title: Wolves 1-1 Portsmouth: Terry Devlin strikes late to earn point for Pompey
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Wolverhampton Wanderers and Portsmouth at Molineux on Tuesday night; Terry Devlin's late goal cancels out Jordan James opener
articles.body:
Four days after Tawanda Chirewa came off the bench to score the winner at Burnley, substitute Jordan James' strike looked like it would prove the difference for Wolves.

But right-back Devlin popped up with a superbly taken equaliser to give Pompey an unlikely share of the spoils.

The scoreline was harsh on Wolves as Chirewa hit the bar and was denied another goal, while Mateus Mane and Fer Lopez missed chances in a dominant second-half performance. Portsmouth failed to hit the target until Devlin struck in the 86th minute.

In a forgettable first half, Andre had the only Wolves chance. The Brazil midfielder lofted a bouncing shot just wide from 25 yards after Devlin beat Marshall Munetsi to head away Mane's cross.

Portsmouth's only chance of the opening half came in the 36th minute. Wolves failed to deal with Adrian Segecic's deep free-kick and after Nasser Djiga missed the header and Ebou Adams' angled effort was blocked, Rocco Shein's low shot was a few feet wide.

Wolves made a double change at half-time to spark some life into the game - Chirewa, Friday's matchwinner at Burnley, and James replaced Sean Neave and Munetsi - and it worked, with a much-improved display.

Chirewa, who scored the winner within 21 seconds of his arrival at Turf Moor, quickly rattled the bar with a tight-angled, rising shot after turning inside his man.

Mane dragged a low, angled drive well wide, then Lopez volleyed wide from Rafiki Said's inviting cross as Wolves continued to probe for the breakthrough.

That came in the 62nd minute from James, who slammed home a fierce low first-time drive after starting the move with a one-two with Lopez, beating Nicolas Schmid at his near post.

Pompey missed a good chance to equalise when Adams headed over substitute Marezi's corner from five yards while substitute Tommy Doyle's teasing cross just missed the sliding Chirewa as Wolves sniffed a second goal.

But Devlin struck when he chested down and volleyed right into the corner of the net after Marezi's free-kick had been headed clear.

Chirewa's low shot was clawed around a post by Schmid as Wolves desperately pushed for a winner at the death and both benches had to be pulled apart at the final whistle as tensions briefly boiled over before order was quickly restored.

articles.title: AFC Wimbledon 0-3 Mansfield
articles.summary: Michael Smith scored twice for Mansfield as they eased to a 3-0 victory against AFC Wimbledon at Plough Lane.
articles.body:
It could have been even more for the Stags as they made it five games unbeaten in League One by making light work of the struggling Dons who suffered a third straight league defeat.

Mansfield had a deserved lead in the 22nd minute when a corner was taken short to Stephen McLaughlin whose cross was headed in by Smith at the back post.

The same combination did the trick again for the visitors five minutes later as another cross from McLaughlin was nodded in by an unmarked Smith.

Wimbledon improved in the second half, but the closest they came to scoring was when Jayden Stockley struck the underside of the crossbar from Aron Sasu's cross.

Instead, Jon Russell made the game safe for Mansfield after 73 minutes with a delightful finish into the top corner.

Rhys Oates had a stoppage-time effort tipped on to the bar by Wimbledon goalkeeper Josef Bursik as the Stags settled for three.

articles.title: Urban Meyer issues a warning to Texas coach Steve Sarkisian
articles.summary: The Texas Longhorns started the season 4-0 and climbed to No. 1 in the country, but back-to-back losses to Oklahoma and Florida have put head coach Steve Sar...
articles.body:
The Texas Longhorns started the season 4-0 and climbed to No. 1 in the country, but back-to-back losses to Oklahoma and Florida have put head coach Steve Sarkisian squarely on the hot seat. Now, one of the most accomplished coaches in college football history thinks that Saturday's game against No. 7 Ole Miss could define Sarkisian's legacy.

Speaking on his podcast this week, three-time national champion Urban Meyer called the matchup with the Rebels "the most important game of Steve Sarkisian's coaching career," warning that a loss would leave Sarkisian known as the coach who "couldn't get it done at Texas."

Texas opened the season by beating Ohio State 24-23 and later knocked off Tennessee on the road, taking over the top spot in the rankings along the way. But the Longhorns lost 27-24 to Oklahoma in the Red River Rivalry, and then fell to Florida by the same score in Austin last weekend.

Things have gotten so rough that Sarkisian didn't rule out benching Arch Manning after the loss to the Gators.

It's the second straight year that Texas has stumbled after entering the season with high expectations. The Longhorns were the preseason No. 1 team in 2025, but they finished 10-3 and missed the College Football Playoff after making back-to-back semifinal appearances in Sarkisian's previous two seasons.

To make matters worse, Texas still has to face Ole Miss and Heisman Trophy contender Trinidad Chambliss, followed by Mississippi State, Missouri, LSU, Arkansas, and Texas A&M.

Meyer laid out the stakes for Sarkisian on The Triple Option , which he co-hosts with Mark Ingram and Rob Stone as he issued a clear warning to the Texas coach.

"This is the most important game of Steve Sarkisian's coaching career," Meyer said on the podcast. "He's had a hell of career, but this one is, this one is a Rubicon… If they lose this one, I mean you are in serious trouble. He won't make the playoff."

Meyer didn't initially think that Sarkisian's job would be on the line, but he did think his reputation would be.

"I don't think it's his job. I think it's just your legacy, though. You're the guy that couldn't get it done at Texas. Because he's been there, he's been there," Meyer said.

But after some more discussion, Meyer came around to the idea that Sarkisian could be fired if Texas misses the playoff again. And he compared the situation to what would happen at Ohio State, where he won a national title in 2014.

"Let's do this. Let's just [imagine]… if this happens at Ohio State: [You're] gone. So maybe you're right," Meyer said. "Could you imagine losing like that, three games? Who's it equal to at Texas? So if all the sudden you lose three at Ohio State, I would always say in my mind, if that ever happened… I didn't think that way, but wow."

Clearly, Meyer isn't the only one who thinks that there's a lot riding on Saturday for Sarkisian. And a loss to Ole Miss would only make the noise in Austin louder.

articles.title: Colorado State's defensive rebuild has DC Kenny McClendon sleeping at work
articles.summary: Colorado State defensive coordinator Kenny McClendon hasn't slept at home in two weeks since taking over play-calling duties, per head coach Jim Mora.
articles.body:
Kenny McClendon has had his hands full over the last few weeks since he took over as Colorado State's defensive coordinator after the firing of Tyson Summers .

It has been so busy that McClendon has moved into Colorado State's football offices in Fort Collins over the past two weeks while working to rebuild the Rams ' defense — at least, according to first-year coach Jim Mora, who shared the story during media availability on Monday, Oct. 19.

"Kenny hasn't been home in two weeks," Mora told reporters. "We took ( Colorado State linebacker coach Jordan Frost-Dixon's office and turned it into a bedroom for Kenny, so he just sleeps there."

McClendon assumed defensive coordinator duties for the rest of the season during the second half of Colorado State's 56-26 loss to Oregon State on Oct. 3, after Mora relieved Summers of his play-calling responsibilities in the first half.

Summers, a second-year defensive coordinator who was retained by Mora from former coach Jay Norvell's staff, did not return to the sidelines for the second half against Oregon State. Colorado State, after opening up the season with a 2-0 record, dropped back-to-back games in which its defense gave up at least 40 points and 500 total yards of offense.

In its first full game with McClendon calling plays last week, the Rams gave up a season-high 66 points and 716 total yards of offense. The Rams defense ranks last in the Pac-12 in scoring defense (43.2 points per game) and total defense (530.3 yards per game). Despite that return, though, Mora believes the defense is in "good hands."

"I know things are in good hands. It's just a matter of building the consistency that's going to help us become a good defense," Mora continued.

Colorado State (2-4 overall, 0-2 in Pac-12 play) hosts San Diego State at 6:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 24.

articles.title: PSG 4-2 Barcelona: European giants play out classic as Hansi Flick's side handed first defeat of the season
articles.summary: Match report as PSG beat Barcelona 4-2 in the UEFA Champions League; European giants put on a classic with 40 attempts at goal; defeat is Barcelona's first of the season
articles.body:
In a game that saw a total of 40 attempts on goal, it was the reigning European champions who were able to outgun the visitors in a contender for match of the season.

The pair traded goals, with Desire Doue's strike and Lucas Hernandez's header each being cancelled out courtesy of youngster Xavi Espart and the irrepressible Lamine Yamal.

Seconds after Barca's number 10 levelled things for a second time, Vitinha restored PSG's lead as Barcelona ran out of gas. Fabian Ruiz put the icing on the cake five minutes later with a tap-in as Hansi Flick side tasted defeat for the first time in 12 games this season.

There were some sour notes on an otherwise exhilarating evening. Ballon d'Or holder Ousmane Dembele came off with a suspected hamstring injury inside the opening 20 minutes. Team-mate Khvicha Kvaratskhelia was also helped off in the second half after picking up a knock.

Dani Olmo was also withdrawn in the first half for Barcelona, who are already struggling with an injury crisis. It adds another blow for the LaLiga leaders, who visit Real Madrid in the first El Clasico of the season on Sunday.

Key moments from a classic at the Parc des Princes...

2: POST! Kvaratskhelia smashes the woodwork in less than 120 seconds.

5: SAVE! Garcia denies Dembele and Doue in quick succession.

10: CHANCE FOR GORDON! Ball drops to Englishman in good position, but he fails to make the most of it.

14: JUST WIDE! Olmo misses target in Barcelona's first meaningful attempt.

19: INJURY! Ballon d'Or holder Dembele comes off with suspected hamstring issue.

25: HUGE MISS! Substitute Torres denied by Garcia from close range.

27: INJURY! Olmo replaced as Barca's injury list grows.

29: CHANCES GALORE! PSG squander three brilliant attempts in a matter of seconds.

38: GOAL! Doue finally puts PSG ahead after Lamine Yamal mistake.

40: SAVE! Nearly immediate response from Barca as Fermin is thwarted by Safanov.

51: SAVE! Hakimi denied as PSG miss more chances.

55: GOAL! PSG punished as Espart equalises.

59: INJURY! Kvaratskhelia is helped off the pitch on the hour.

71: POST! Torres misses again as he strikes the post from close range!

72: GOAL! A set-piece does the job as Hernandez's header restores PSG's lead.

79: GOAL! Lamine Yamal smashes Barca level from a tight angle.

81: GOAL! Vitinha hits back immediately from edge of the box.

86: GOAL! Ruiz seals the deal as Barca run out of steam.

Analysis from Sky Sports' Callum Bishop:

"I covered PSG's 5-4 win over Bayern Munich last season. It was a breathless game and one of the greatest I had ever witnessed.

"While tonight might not quite have been at that level, it was in a very similar bracket. Two of the best teams in the world with full belief in themselves and only one intention: outscore the other.

"No one could've blamed Barcelona if they came to the French capital and decided they were going to shut up shop and try to stop the potent PSG attack.

"Their approach was the complete opposite. They had faith that their attack was as lethal. In the end, they fell short, but they can hold their heads high.

"As a neutral, these are the types of games you dream of watching. It makes you feel things only free-flowing football can.

"If you want a demonstration of what two heavyweight giants playing each other should look like, it is this. Blow for blow, haymaker for haymaker.
